name: What's the difference between a whole-home remodel and a home addition?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a whole-home remodel and a home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A whole-home remodel primarily focuses on updating and reconfiguring existing spaces within your home's current footprint. This can involve changing layouts, upgrading finishes, and updating systems like plumbing and electrical. A home addition, on the other hand, involves expanding the physical size of your house by adding new square footage, such as an extra room, a second story, or an expanded living area. While a remodel improves existing space, an addition creates entirely new space, often leading to more extensive structural work and higher costs.
acceptedAnswer.description: A whole-home remodel updates existing spaces, while a home addition expands your home's physical size by adding new square footage.
